segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for taking the call, Dana. And thanks for moving it from 10:30. I had a cleanup block in the CRM that ran long, so I appreciate the flexibility.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: No problem. I’ve got about 20 minutes. We’re still looking at 42 seats for the customer success team, with maybe 8 more in Q2 if support joins.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it, 42 to start. On the pricing sheet that puts you at $68 per seat per month on annual, so roughly $34,272 for the year before the onboarding package.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. The onboarding was the $4,800 line item, right? Finance asked if that can be invoiced separately from the subscription.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, we can split that. Subscription on the main annual invoice, onboarding as a one-time services invoice. If you want a March 18 go-live, we’d want signatures by February 23 so the implementation team can get the kickoff scheduled.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That timing works. Contract-wise, legal is asking for a 30-day termination for convenience. I know you said that’s not standard.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Right, standard is annual non-cancelable. What I can probably get approved is a 60-day termination right after the first year, plus a cap on the renewal increase at 5%.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Send that over. Also, our procurement lead, Mark, can join today at 3 if you’re free. He’ll ask about payment terms and the security exhibit.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: I’m tied up at 3 getting the order form fields matched for deal desk, but I can do 4:15 and keep it to 25 minutes. Payment terms would be net 30, and the security exhibit is already in the paper package.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: 4:15 is fine. Please include the split invoice language and the 5% renewal cap in the version you send before then.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send the redline and the quote summary by 2:30, and then we can use the 4:15 to get Mark comfortable on the last procurement items.
